title: staggered-eviction-hedge-and-degraded-kv-fastpath-fallback
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Introduces a staggered node eviction hedge, a degraded KV fastpath that serves stale-but-ok entries during mass drains, and an SLO-aware gate to avoid cascading evictions. Adds observability and a safe rollout plan.
description:
Context and motivation: During a recent regional degradation incident we observed cascade eviction behavior where simultaneous KV cache drains caused a wave of cold-starts and p99 token latencies that violated SLOs. This PR implements an eviction-hedge mechanism that staggers node drain actions, plus a degraded KV fastpath that can serve recently-stale cache entries (with conservative TTL) while background resyncs repopulate caches. The goal is graceful degradation (maintain correctness while avoiding SLO spikes) and to reduce the probability of a large-scale regional failover when capacity is transiently constrained.

What this PR changes (summary): 
- New eviction hedging controller that coordinates drain timelines across nodes in a region; hedging introduces jittered drain windows and a global admission gate when p99 latency or error budget is at risk.
- Degraded KV fastpath: cache read shim that can return stale values marked with served_from_stale flag; stale responses are only allowed when background resync is active and the entry age < configurable stale_ttl_ms.
- Opportunistic staggered KV-sync: when a node is marked for drain, instead of immediate full sync, it performs prioritized, rate-limited KV prefetches for hot keys and defers low-priority syncs to avoid saturating egress.
- SLO-enforcer integration: eviction controller queries the SLO enforcer to decide whether to delay or serialize new drains; adds config knobs to override in emergency.
- Metrics and dashboards: new meters for staggered-drain-windows, stale-served-count, stale-resync-latency, and hedged-eviction-delay.
- Tests, load tests, and rollout artifacts: unit tests, integration test harness updates, and a perf-canary manifest used during canary rollout.

Review conversation (highlights, chronological compressed into a single string):

Two asks: (1) please add a guard to ensure stale fastpath cannot be used for security-sensitive objects, and (2) document the exact semantics of stale_ttl and served_from_stale flag so downstream services can treat it correctly."
- Aisha (reply): "Added a per-key allowlist and a `sensitive_key_regex` config that bypasses stale serving; expanded docs section to clarify served_from_stale and its header propagation. Also added unit test for sensitive key behavior."

- Claire Duval (review): "Lint and a small race in staggered_sync.go; suggests adding a sync.Once for background resync bootstrap."
- Aisha (reply): "Fixed race, addressed lint; reran unit tests and perf canary."
- Miguel (approval): "Approving after seeing the canary results. Recommend watchlist on next three releases for p99 anomalies."

CI and checks: 
- Initial run: lint failed (long lines in docs) -> fixed in commit 3
- Second run: unit tests pass, integration suite partly flaky on unrelated infra test -> reran
- Final run: all checks green, canary smoke passed with no SLO regressions; perf-canary metrics show p99 improvement under simulated node drains.

Rollout plan / migration notes: 
- Feature gated behind `eviction_hedge_enabled` (default false) and `stale_fastpath_enabled` (default false).
- Canary: enable in a single low-traffic region (us-west-2) for 24h, monitor stale_served_count and p99 latency.
- Gradual ramp: 10% nodes -> 33% -> 100% over 48h if metrics remain healthy.
- Rollback: flip feature flags off; controller includes an immediate drain flush path to complete in-flight drains.

Why this is different from other mitigations: Existing mitigations focused on outright load shedding or circuit breakers that reject requests. This change favors transient degraded responses (serve stale) and serialized drains to preserve availability and avoid mass cold-starts. It trades freshness for latency stability in a controlled, observable way.

Follow-ups:

- Auto-tuning experiment to correlate stale_served_count with long-term model quality metrics (if degraded responses are downstream-validated).
